newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS-Creditanstalt posts record Q1, appoints new CEO.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Creditanstalt posts record Q1, appoints new CEO.

text.p: Austria's Creditanstalt said on Tuesday first quarter group operating profit hit a record high and offered an even more upbeat outlook for the full year as its chief executive for the past nine years took final leave.

The bank, recently fallen under the control of market leader Bank Austria, said operating profit in the first three months rose 31 percent to 2.11 billion schillings ($173.2 million), boosted by strong international business and treasury operations.
For the full year, Creditanstalt said more good news was on the way.
"The very good operating profit of the first months of the current year makes us expect a further gain in full-year net profit compared to 1996," it said in a shareholders' letter.
Last year, Creditanstalt reported a full year net profit of 2.93 billion schillings, up 35 percent from the previous year.
The bank said the first-quarter figures did not include a "net capital gain" of about 1.3 billion schillings from the sale of a 32.8 percent stake in machine maker Maschinenfabrik Andritz last month.

In a statement released ahead of its annual shareholders' meeting, it said first quarter operating earnings rose to 5.31 billion schillings from 4.58 billion a year earlier, while operating expenses increased to 3.20 billion schillings from 2.97 billion a year ago.
Total assets grew 7.3 percent to 737.58 billion at the end of March, it added.

Creditanstalt is controlled by Bank Austria, which in January acquired the state's majority stake in the country's second largest bank for 17.2 billion schillings in cash. Bank Austria effectively controls some 70 percent of Creditanstalt's voting capital.

Creditanstalt's supervisory board, which convened after the shareholder's meeting, voted career banker Erich Hampel to succeed Guido Schmidt-Chiari, who resigned as the bank's chief executive following the takeover.
"The new chief executive Erich Hampel will start in his position on May 15," the bank said in a statement.
Hampel, 47, currently chairs the board of postal savings bank PSK, which is due for partial privatisation this year.
Schmidt-Chiari was one of the most vociferous opponents of the sale of Creditanstalt to Bank Austria.
Board member Alarich Fenyves, who has been in charge of the bank's international business, was named as Hampel's number two, the bank added.
Creditanstalt's supervisory boared is chaired by Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa.
Shareholders earlier voted to change the official name of the bank to Creditanstalt AG from Creditanstalt-Bankverein AG.

According to the blueprint of the merger deal which ended Europe's longest runnig privatisation saga, Bank Austria will keep Creditanstalt as an independent unit for at least five years. ($ = 12.18 Austrian Schillings)
